subject: [PATCH v4 20/21] iomap: pass iomap_iter_next_fn directly instead of struct iomap_ops

reviews.author: Darrick Wong
reviews.summary: Reviewer Darrick Wong suggested using a macro to define the forward declaration of iomap_next functions, specifically proposing the DECLARE_IOMAP_NEXT(name) macro, but left open to alternative opinions.
reviews.raw_body:
I wonder, would it make more sense to have a macro to define the forward
declaration?  e.g.

#define DECLARE_IOMAP_NEXT(name) \
	int name(...)

DECLARE_IOMAP_NEXT(xfs_buffered_write_iomap_next);

Hm?

Though feel free to say "declaration macros suck!" because they do.
Reviewed-by: "Darrick J. Wong" <djwong@kernel.org>

--D

2026-07-27.patch_summary: This patch simplifies the iomap code by removing the struct iomap_ops, which only contained a single function pointer, and instead passes the iomap_iter_next_fn directly to various functions. This change is made possible because all filesystems now implement ->iomap_next() and have removed legacy fallbacks. The patch also renames the ops field in the iomap_iter tracepoint to next for consistency.
